title.en: Gerund or Infinitive (I enjoy swimming / I want to swim)
title.es: Gerundio o infinitivo (I enjoy swimming / I want to swim)

text.en: When two verbs follow each other, the second can have two forms in English: -ing (gerund) or to + base verb (infinitive). The first verb decides which one: after “enjoy” comes -ing (“I enjoy swimming”), after “want” comes to + verb (“I want to swim”). Spanish does not help here: it always uses the infinitive (“me encanta nadar”, “quiero nadar”), so you have to learn this verb by verb in English.
text.es: Cuando dos verbos van seguidos, el segundo puede tener dos formas en inglés: -ing (gerundio) o to + verbo base (infinitivo). El primer verbo decide cuál: después de «enjoy» va -ing («I enjoy swimming»), después de «want» va to + verbo («I want to swim»). El español no ayuda aquí: siempre usa el infinitivo («me encanta nadar», «quiero nadar»), por eso hay que aprenderlo verbo por verbo en inglés.

text.en: After some verbs there is always -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, keep, mind, practice, suggest, give up.
text.es: Después de algunos verbos siempre va -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, keep, mind, practice, suggest, give up.

tr.en: I enjoy listening to music.
He finished doing his homework.

text.en: After a preposition there is always -ing, where Spanish uses the infinitive: before leaving, thanks for coming, interested in learning, good at cooking.
text.es: Después de una preposición siempre va -ing, donde el español usa el infinitivo: before leaving, thanks for coming, interested in learning, good at cooking.

tr.en: I'm interested in learning English.

examples.es: Before leaving, he locked the door.

tr.en: Before leaving, he locked the door.
tr.es: Antes de salir, cerró la puerta.

text.en: The -ing form can also be the subject of a sentence: “Swimming is fun.” In English the infinitive is rarer here.
text.es: La forma -ing también puede ser el sujeto de una oración: «Swimming is fun.» En inglés el infinitivo es menos frecuente aquí.

examples.es: Walking every day is good for your health.

tr.en: Walking every day is good for your health.
tr.es: Caminar todos los días es bueno para la salud.

tr.en: Swimming is fun.

text.en: After other verbs there is to + base verb: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, promise, would like, can’t afford, refuse.
text.es: Después de otros verbos va to + verbo base: want, need, decide, hope, plan, learn, promise, would like, can’t afford, refuse.

examples.es: She wants to be a doctor.

tr.en: She wants to be a doctor.
We decided to leave early.

text.en: Expressing a purpose: to + base verb (“in order to…”). The Spanish “para + infinitivo” is to in English, not “for”: “I went to the market to buy fruit.”
text.es: Expresar un propósito: to + verbo base («para…»). El «para + infinitivo» español es to en inglés, no «for»: «I went to the market to buy fruit.»

examples.es: I went to the market to buy fruit.

tr.en: I went to the market to buy fruit.
tr.es: Fui al mercado a comprar fruta.

examples.es: We can't afford to buy a new car.

tr.en: We can't afford to buy a new car.
tr.es: No podemos permitirnos comprar un carro nuevo.

title.en: The same verb, a different meaning

text.en: Stop + -ing: to quit doing something. Stop + to + base verb: to pause in order to do something.
text.es: Stop + -ing: dejar de hacer algo. Stop + to + verbo base: detenerse para hacer algo.

examples.es: We stopped talking when the teacher came in.

tr.en: We stopped talking when the teacher came in.
tr.es: Dejamos de hablar cuando entró el maestro.

examples.es: She stopped to buy a coffee.

tr.en: She stopped to buy a coffee.
tr.es: Se detuvo para comprar un café.

text.en: Remember + -ing: to recall something that happened. Remember + to + base verb: not to forget to do it.
text.es: Remember + -ing: recordar algo que pasó. Remember + to + verbo base: no olvidar hacerlo.

examples.es: I remember meeting him last year.

tr.en: I remember meeting him last year.
tr.es: Recuerdo haberlo conocido el año pasado.

tr.en: Remember to close the door!

text.en: The Spanish “me encanta nadar” is not “I enjoy to swim” in English, but “I enjoy swimming”. After enjoy, finish, avoid, mind there is always -ing.
text.es: El «me encanta nadar» español no es «I enjoy to swim» en inglés, sino «I enjoy swimming». Después de enjoy, finish, avoid, mind siempre va -ing.

text.en: After a preposition use -ing, not the infinitive: not “thanks for to help”, but “thanks for helping”; not “interested in to learn”, but “interested in learning”. The to form only comes when to belongs to the verb (want to).
text.es: Después de una preposición usa -ing, no el infinitivo: no «thanks for to help», sino «thanks for helping»; no «interested in to learn», sino «interested in learning». La forma con to solo aparece cuando to forma parte del verbo (want to).

text.en: A purpose “para + infinitivo” is to + base verb in English, not “for + verb”: not “I went there for buy”, but “I went there to buy”. After for comes a noun or -ing (“for shopping”).
text.es: El propósito «para + infinitivo» es to + verbo base en inglés, no «for + verbo»: no «I went there for buy», sino «I went there to buy». Después de for va un sustantivo o -ing («for shopping»).

speak.en: When two verbs follow each other, the second one can have two forms in English: «ing» or «to» plus the base verb. The first verb decides which one. After «enjoy», «finish», «avoid» comes «ing»: «I enjoy swimming». After «want», «decide», «hope» comes «to» plus a verb: «I want to swim». After a preposition there is always «ing»: «I'm interested in learning English». A purpose is «to» plus a verb: «I went to the market to buy fruit». «Stop» has two meanings: «We stopped talking» and «She stopped to buy a coffee».
speak.es: Cuando dos verbos van seguidos, el segundo puede tener dos formas en inglés: «ing» o «to» más verbo base. El primer verbo decide cuál. Después de «enjoy», «finish», «avoid» va «ing»: «I enjoy swimming». Después de «want», «decide», «hope» va «to» más verbo: «I want to swim». Después de una preposición siempre va «ing»: «I'm interested in learning English». Un propósito es «to» más verbo: «I went to the market to buy fruit». «Stop» tiene dos significados: «We stopped talking» y «She stopped to buy a coffee».

why.es: Después de enjoy va -ing: enjoy listening.

listen.en: The base verb after enjoy is incorrect; you need the -ing form (listening).
listen.es: El verbo base después de enjoy es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (listening).

to listen.en: The Spanish “me encanta escuchar” tempts you to use to, but after enjoy comes -ing.
to listen.es: El «me encanta escuchar» español tienta a usar to, pero después de enjoy va -ing.

tr.en: I enjoy listening to music.

why.en: After want comes to + base verb: want to be.
why.es: Después de want va to + verbo base: want to be.

being.en: After want comes not an -ing form; you need to + base verb (to be).
being.es: Después de want no va una forma -ing; hace falta to + verbo base (to be).

be.en: After want the to cannot be left out; not “wants be” but wants to be.
be.es: Después de want no se puede omitir to; no «wants be» sino wants to be.

tr.en: She wants to be a doctor.

why.es: Después de finish va -ing: finished doing.

do.en: The base verb after finish is incorrect; you need the -ing form (doing).
do.es: El verbo base después de finish es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (doing).

to do.en: The Spanish “terminó de hacer” tempts you to use to, but after finish comes -ing.
to do.es: El «terminó de hacer» español tienta a usar to, pero después de finish va -ing.

tr.en: He finished doing his homework.
tr.es: Él terminó de hacer su tarea.

why.en: After decide comes to + base verb: decided to leave.
why.es: Después de decide va to + verbo base: decided to leave.

leaving.en: After decide comes not an -ing form; you need to + base verb (to leave).
leaving.es: Después de decide no va una forma -ing; hace falta to + verbo base (to leave).

leave.en: After decide the to cannot be left out; not “decided leave” but decided to leave.
leave.es: Después de decide no se puede omitir to; no «decided leave» sino decided to leave.

tr.en: We decided to leave early.

why.en: After a preposition (in) comes -ing: interested in learning.
why.es: Después de una preposición (in) va -ing: interested in learning.

learn.en: The base verb after a preposition is incorrect; you need the -ing form (learning).
learn.es: El verbo base después de una preposición es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (learning).

to learn.en: The Spanish “interesado en aprender” tempts you to use to, but after a preposition comes -ing.
to learn.es: El «interesado en aprender» español tienta a usar to, pero después de una preposición va -ing.

tr.en: I'm interested in learning English.

why.en: After the preposition for comes -ing: for helping.
why.es: Después de la preposición for va -ing: for helping.

help.en: The base verb after for is incorrect; you need the -ing form (helping).
help.es: El verbo base después de for es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (helping).

to help.en: After for there is no to; for is a preposition, and after a preposition comes -ing.
to help.es: Después de for no va to; for es una preposición, y después de una preposición va -ing.

tr.en: Thank you for helping me.

items.sentence: Before ___ the house, he locked the door.

why.en: After the preposition before comes -ing: before leaving.
why.es: Después de la preposición before va -ing: before leaving.

leave.en: The base verb after before is incorrect; you need the -ing form (leaving).
leave.es: El verbo base después de before es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (leaving).

to leave.en: The Spanish “antes de salir” tempts you to use to, but after before comes -ing.
to leave.es: El «antes de salir» español tienta a usar to, pero después de before va -ing.

tr.en: Before leaving the house, he locked the door.
tr.es: Antes de salir de la casa, él cerró la puerta con llave.

items.sentence: I went to the market ___ some fruit.

why.en: Expressing a purpose: to + base verb: to buy.
why.es: Para expresar un propósito: to + verbo base: to buy.

for buy.en: “For buy” is incorrect; in English a purpose is to + base verb, not for + verb.
for buy.es: «For buy» es incorrecto; en inglés un propósito es to + verbo base, no for + verbo.

buying.en: To express a purpose use not -ing but to + base verb (to buy).
buying.es: Para expresar un propósito se usa no -ing sino to + verbo base (to buy).

tr.en: I went to the market to buy some fruit.
tr.es: Fui al mercado a comprar algo de fruta.

items.sentence: ___ every day is good for your health.

why.en: As a subject the -ing form is used: Walking every day is good.
why.es: Como sujeto se usa la forma -ing: Walking every day is good.

Walk.en: The base verb does not stand as a subject at the start; you need the -ing form (Walking).
Walk.es: El verbo base no va como sujeto al principio; hace falta la forma -ing (Walking).

To walking.en: “To walking” is an incorrect mix: either To walk or Walking; as a subject Walking is the usual form.
To walking.es: «To walking» es una mezcla incorrecta: o To walk o Walking; como sujeto lo habitual es Walking.

tr.en: Walking every day is good for your health.
tr.es: Caminar todos los días es bueno para la salud.

why.es: Después de avoid va -ing: avoid eating.

to eat.en: After avoid comes not to + base verb but an -ing form (eating).
to eat.es: Después de avoid no va to + verbo base sino una forma -ing (eating).

eat.en: The base verb after avoid is incorrect; you need the -ing form (eating).
eat.es: El verbo base después de avoid es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (eating).

tr.en: I avoid eating meat.

why.en: After hope comes to + base verb: hope to see.
why.es: Después de hope va to + verbo base: hope to see.

seeing.en: After hope comes not an -ing form; you need to + base verb (to see).
seeing.es: Después de hope no va una forma -ing; hace falta to + verbo base (to see).

see.en: After hope the to cannot be left out; not “hope see” but hope to see.
see.es: Después de hope no se puede omitir to; no «hope see» sino hope to see.

tr.en: I hope to see you soon.

items.sentence: The teacher came in, so we stopped ___.

why.en: We quit talking: stop + -ing, stopped talking.
why.es: Dejamos de hablar: stop + -ing, stopped talking.

to talk.en: Stopped to talk would mean we paused in order to talk; here we quit talking.
to talk.es: Stopped to talk significaría que nos detuvimos para hablar; aquí dejamos de hablar.

talk.en: The base verb after stopped is incorrect; you need either -ing or to + base verb.
talk.es: El verbo base después de stopped es incorrecto; hace falta -ing o to + verbo base.

tr.en: The teacher came in, so we stopped talking.
tr.es: El maestro entró, así que dejamos de platicar.

items.sentence: She stopped ___ a coffee at the shop.

why.en: She paused in order to buy a coffee: stop + to + base verb, stopped to buy.
why.es: Se detuvo para comprar un café: stop + to + verbo base, stopped to buy.

buying.en: Stopped buying would mean she quit buying; here she paused in order to buy something.
buying.es: Stopped buying significaría que dejó de comprar; aquí se detuvo para comprar algo.

buy.en: The base verb after stopped is incorrect; you need either -ing or to + base verb.
buy.es: El verbo base después de stopped es incorrecto; hace falta -ing o to + verbo base.

tr.en: She stopped to buy a coffee at the shop.
tr.es: Ella se detuvo a comprar un café en la tienda.

why.en: I recall that I met him: remember + -ing, remember meeting.
why.es: Recuerdo haberlo conocido: remember + -ing, remember meeting.

to meet.en: Remember to meet would mean not to forget to do it; here it is about a memory of the past.
to meet.es: Remember to meet significaría no olvidar hacerlo; aquí se trata de un recuerdo del pasado.

meet.en: The base verb after remember is incorrect; you need either -ing or to + base verb.
meet.es: El verbo base después de remember es incorrecto; hace falta -ing o to + verbo base.

tr.en: I remember meeting him last year.
tr.es: Recuerdo haberlo conocido el año pasado.

why.en: Do not forget to do it: remember + to + base verb, remember to close.
why.es: No olvides hacerlo: remember + to + verbo base, remember to close.

closing.en: Remember closing refers to a memory of the past; the reminder (“don’t forget”) is to + base verb.
closing.es: Remember closing se refiere a un recuerdo del pasado; el recordatorio («no olvides») es to + verbo base.

close.en: The base verb after remember is incorrect; you need either -ing or to + base verb.
close.es: El verbo base después de remember es incorrecto; hace falta -ing o to + verbo base.

tr.en: Remember to close the door!

why.en: After good at comes -ing: good at speaking.
why.es: Después de good at va -ing: good at speaking.

speak.en: The base verb after the preposition at is incorrect; you need the -ing form (speaking).
speak.es: El verbo base después de la preposición at es incorrecto; hace falta la forma -ing (speaking).

to speak.en: At is a preposition; after a preposition comes not to + base verb but -ing.
to speak.es: At es una preposición; después de una preposición no va to + verbo base sino -ing.

tr.en: She is good at speaking English.

buying.es: Después de afford no va una forma -ing; hace falta to + verbo base (to buy).

buy.en: After afford the to cannot be left out; not “afford buy” but afford to buy.

tr.en: We can't afford to buy a new car.
